articles.title: STILL: the first esport for lying down
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady I built the first esport for lying down. There is no controller. No keyboard. No skill tree. You give the br…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built I built the first esport for lying down. There is no controller. No keyboard. No skill tree. You give the browser permission to use your webcam, lie down, and try to stay completely still for 60 seconds while a referee powered by Gemma watches your skeleton and quietly judges you. That is the whole game. One rule: do not move. It sounds easy until the referee notices that your left wrist has been twitching and decides to do something about it. First it throws a dry little insult. Then it picks the joint you are least able to control and aims a temptation straight at it. A fly. An itch. A notification. If you move that exact joint, you lose double points.
articles.author: Mudit Palvadi

articles.body: Q1 (web flag): THM{ok_you_f0und_w3b_fl4g_6cbe2bc} Q2 (encryption key): THM{Traditional_Own_Crypto_is_Always_Surprising!_and_this_hopefully_is_not_easy_to_crack_e41d20b5b0989cac65ed4a090cace944bf30e6d3ab88f9d447f52fd2140525b9} A PHP app rolls its own "military-grade" cookie encryption: each 8-byte block of user:User-Agent:ENC_SECRET_KEY is run through crypt() with a single 2-character salt, and the results are concatenated. articles.title: Black October hit PHP, npm and PyPI. So I built a system that catches it in my app before I ship, with the fix ready
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady This month already has a name: Black October. In three weeks, npm releases shipped with malware (one of them…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady This month already has a name: Black October . In three weeks, npm releases shipped with malware (one of them a worm), a poisoned LiteLLM release on PyPI carried a credential stealer, and PHP patched PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), two bugs that let a stranger take over a PHP server with no bug in the site's own code ( CNBC , a running list ). On a week like that, the only question that matters is: are we in it? The trick that worries me most is older. In August, a worm called ChainDrop went through more than 400 npm packages. Stealing tokens wasn't the clever part.

articles.body: Most landing-page advice comes as a template: a hero of a certain height, three feature cards, a testimonial strip, a pricing table, an FAQ. Templates are quick to fill in, but they don't tell you whether the page answers the questions its visitors actually have. That's the gap the Universal Landing Page Guide (ULPG) tries to fill. It's an open guide that I'm working on with the other ULPG contributors, and this post introduces what's in it, who it's for and how to use it, including with an AI agent. What ULPG is In the README's words, ULPG is "an open guide for people and AI agents designing, building, and reviewing landing pages.

articles.body: Doctor Who has never shied away from showing the Doctor at his worst . In “A Good Man Goes to War,” Eleven (Matt Smith) realizes that his choices have made him nearly as monstrous as his enemies. In “The Waters of Mars,” Ten (David Tennant) is still reeling from the loss of his most recent companion, Donna Noble (Catherine Tate), and determined to win for once. articles.title: 50 Years Later, the Best War Series of All Time Is Still Unlike Anything Else on TV
articles.excerpt: MASH blended humor and heartbreak to create unforgettable characters and deliver one of television's most memorable finales.
articles.body: When Robert Altman's M*A*S*H arrived in theaters in 1970, its irreverent approach to the Korean War was unlike anything audiences had seen before. The film followed army surgeons who used practical jokes, alcohol, and a disregard for military authority to maintain their sanity while treating the wounded. Two years later, CBS adapted the film into a television series that retained its anarchic spirit but accomplished something the movie couldn't: It gave audiences time to get to know these characters.

articles.body: SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast. The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket , which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California). The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). articles.body: NASA just gave us our best look yet at its Artemis III moon-lander test flight. The agency laid out a detailed concept of operations for Artemis III today (Oct. 23) during a press conference at Kennedy Space Center , stressing how important the flight is to its moon plans and how challenging it will be to make everything go right. "We're launching three of the most powerful rockets in the world, and undertaking what is likely the most complicated launch campaign ever undertaken," Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager, said during today's event, which lasted more than two hours. articles.body: 7 Min Read NASA, Partners Accelerate Lander Development for 2028 Moon Missions As NASA returns humans to the lunar surface and establishes a long-term presence on our closest celestial neighbor, the agency and commercial human landing system providers Blue Origin and SpaceX have streamlined the designs and changed both concepts of operations for its future crewed landers. Since NASA established initial contracts with Blue Origin and SpaceX for crewed missions to the Moon, the agency has redefined Artemis III to demonstrate rendezvous and docking capabilities between test versions of landers from each provider and the agency’s Orion spacecraft in low Earth orbit next year.

articles.title: NASA’s Artemis III Mission to Test Future Moon Lander Operations
articles.excerpt: Before astronauts return to the lunar surface, NASA will first conduct one of the most ambitious and complex test missions in the agency’s history. Launching in 2027, Artemis III will send NASA astron…
articles.body: Before astronauts return to the lunar surface, NASA will first conduct one of the most ambitious and complex test missions in the agency’s history.  Launching in 2027, Artemis III will send NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, Andre Douglas, and ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano aboard the Orion spacecraft into low Earth orbit to perform a series of demonstrations with test versions, or test articles, of human landing systems being developed by industry partners Blue Origin and SpaceX. During the planned 14-day mission, crews and flight controllers will practice the rendezvous, docking, habitation, and operational procedures that will be essential when Artemis astronauts begin landing near the Moon’s South Pole in 2028.

articles.title: Some iPhone Duo screens aren’t making it through day one
articles.excerpt: Unlucky early buyers say their iPhone Duo screens are cracking after just a few unfolds.
articles.body: TL;DR Some early iPhone Duo owners are reporting cracked inner screens, with damage appearing near the crease. One owner says their screen broke after fewer than 20 unfolds, and Apple replaced the phone immediately. The cause and scale remain unclear, and it’s too early to establish whether there’s a broader design flaw. It’s October 23, and arguably the most-hyped smartphone of the year is finally starting to reach customers. Apple’s iPhone Duo is available starting today, and although supply is thin and delivery estimates unsightly , there’s a bigger reason that mars what should be a celebratory launch day. Early iPhone Duo buyers are facing problems with the new foldable’s hinge, with some reporting that the phone’s inner screens cracked after a handful of folds and unfolds.

articles.title: This launcher was made for your dual-screen Android handheld
articles.excerpt: Using a Retroid Pocket Duo or AYN Thor handheld? This Android launcher was made for you.
articles.body: Credit: Nick Fernandez / Android Authority TL;DR A developer has created a new Android launcher made for single- and double-screen gaming. The Android frontend is called “Blip” and it works with AYN, Retroid, AYANEO, and Anbernic devices. It also works on phones, tablets, and other devices that run Android 12 or later. The developer is also working on a feature called Blip Cloud, which backs up your saves and syncs them between different devices. The Android handheld world is full of double-screen devices, like the Retroid Pocket Duo Lite Plus and AYN Thor . Anbernic even has a new one that could start shipping in December . While these devices already come with an Android frontend, you don’t have to settle for what came pre-installed.
